thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and TLS handshake failures observed on prod-gateway (nodes: gateway-1/gateway-2). p50 handshake-failures spike from 0.1% -> 12% in last 3m. Paging @ops-oncall and @alice.sre. Links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/gateway/handshakes (graphs)
alice.sre: Acknowledged. I'm oncall. What's the scope? Any customer-facing errors or API latencies? If there's a cert issue, is it mTLS or client side?
raj.sre: I'm seeing a lot of `TLS_HANDSHAKE_ERROR` in the edge logs and proxies returning 502/524. Quick grep on gateway-2 shows repeated "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" and "certificate has expired" entries.
kevin.net: From the network side, upstream connectivity is fine. No routing flaps. TLS handshake failures started at 2765439800-ish. Could be cert chain problem. 
maria.pm: Product: customers in EU and US are seeing increased error percentages. A few high-traffic tenants reported 502s. No SLO breaches yet but trending.
raj.sre: Running an openssl probe against gateway VIP:
```
openssl s_client -connect gw-prod:443 -showcerts -servername api.redwood.example.com
```
Output shows chain ends at an intermediate cert with `Not After: Feb 28 23:59:59 2026 GMT` -> expired.
alice.sre: That matches the logs. Which cert? Edge uses cert set `edge-2026-q1` deployed by cert-rotator service.
deploy-bot: rotator-job-20260301 returned status=FAILED at 2765439605. Error: `PUT s3://certs-uploads/edge-2026-q1.pem 403 AccessDenied` (see logs: https://logs.redwood/rotator/2765439605)
raj.sre: Looks like rotator couldn't upload updated chain to S3, so the edge hosts kept serving the old chain where the intermediate is expired. We'll need a live mitigation: either push a manual chain, enable fallback routing to secondary gateway pool with valid chain, or roll traffic to older tenants.
ops-oncall: Suggest manual push to rotator and restart the rotator agent on edge nodes to pick up new chain. Also we can set temporary routing rule to steer traffic away from gateway-2 (which has the stale chain) to gateway-3 which still has valid chain.
alice.sre: Action plan: 1) Confirm which hosts have expired chain. 2) If safe, push new chain manually to rotator S3 and trigger a refresh. 3) If push fails or takes >10m, apply traffic steer to reduce customer impact. I'll coordinate handoff after mitigation.
kevin.net: I can apply traffic steer. Suggest 30% -> gateway-3, 70% -> gateway-1, disable gateway-2 for new connections. Applying now.
kevin.net: `trafficctl set-route gateway-vip --steer gateway-2=0,gateway-1=0.7,gateway-3=0.3` -> applied. Monitoring.
maria.pm: Noted — product team will prepare a short customer update if errors persist beyond 15m.
raj.sre: Manual S3 upload attempt (from bastion):
```
aws s3 cp ./edge-2026-q1-fullchain.pem s3://certs-uploads/edge-2026-q1.pem --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```
Result: `AccessDenied` same as rotator. Investigating IAM permissions.
alice.sre: Can we use the rotator's fallback artifact store? There is an internal artifact bucket `certs-backup` with different IAM. Trying a copy there.
raj.sre: Copied chain to certs-backup and triggered local rotator refresh on gateway-3 and gateway-1:
```
ssh root@gateway-3 'systemctl restart cert-rotator && journalctl -u cert-rotator -n 200'
```
Rotator on gateway-3 picked up new chain and reloaded. gateway-1 also success. gateway-2 still has old chain (rotator can't update due to node agent pulling from main bucket).
ops-oncall: Observability update: 5xx rate dropped from 9% -> 2.5% after steer.
kevin.net: Continuing to hold gateway-2 at 0 for new connections. We should bring it back only after we can push updated chain.
maria.pm: Customers: errors decreased for most tenants. A few heavy tenants still report intermittent 502s (likely existing connections to gateway-2). We'll keep monitoring.
deploy-bot: rotator-job-resubmit created job 2765440200 to retry upload with support ticket on S3 permissions. Logged: https://jobs.redwood/rotator/2765440200
alice.sre: Next steps: 1) Ops verifies rotator S3 IAM fix with infra. 2) Re-run upload flow and validate all gateways have the new chain. 3) Gradually reintroduce gateway-2 traffic and observe handshake error metrics for 30m. 4) Post-incident ticket and postmortem.
raj.sre: Infra discovered a recently rotated KMS policy that removed the rotator service principal from the s3:PutObject access. Infra is reverting the policy now.
infra (via alice.sre): Policy revert applied. Please re-run rotator upload.
raj.sre: Re-run of rotator upload succeeds now. Rotator reports `uploaded edge-2026-q1.pem` at 2765440345 and edge nodes started refreshing.
kevin.net: Reintroducing gateway-2 traffic in steps: set-route to gateway-2=0.2,gateway-1=0.5,gateway-3=0.3
ops-oncall: Handshake-failures metric now down to baseline (0.15%). 5xxs at 0.7%. No new customer tickets in last 10m.
alice.sre: Good mitigation. We'll leave monitoring window open for 60m and then close the pager if stable. Assigning postmortem to @maria.pm and @raj.sre. Please include timeline, root cause (KMS/IAM policy rotation broke rotator uploads -> stale intermediate -> expired chain), customer impact, mitigation steps, and follow-ups: org process for KMS policy changes, rotator upload validation alert.
maria.pm: I'll draft the customer impact note and start the postmortem doc. Quick note: create a short KB for emergency manual chain push and traffic-steer runbook.
raj.sre: Added runbook PR: https://git.redwood/runbooks/cert-rotator-emergency/PR-142
alice.sre: Thanks all. Handoff to next oncall in 20m: @raj.sre will take over monitoring while I wrap up. If anything spikes, re-pager.
ops-oncall: Handoff ack. Flagging for post-incident review with infra and security (KMS policy change).
incident-bot: Incident resolved -> mitigation in place, metrics normalized. Pager closed by alice.sre at 2765440519. Please file postmortem within 72h.
